Service: Physical therapy, therapeutic exercise (CPT 97110), visits 21-24
Denial notice date: September 14, 2026

This letter is a formal internal appeal of the denial dated September 14, 2026 for physical therapy visits 21 through 24 (CPT 97110). The plan stated that the benefit limit was exhausted. I ask Sunbelt Community Health to review this decision again and to overturn the denial. This appeal is filed within the time allowed after receipt of the notice [[cite:fed.internal_appeal.filing_window]].

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text:
I received outpatient physical therapy at Coastal Physical Therapy & Rehab on August 25, 2026 and September 3, 2026. The services were billed as therapeutic exercise, CPT 97110, described in the notice as visits 21 through 24.

The amount billed was $640.00. The plan paid $0.00. The notice does not state an amount of patient responsibility.

The reason given in the denial, quoted word for word, is: "Benefit limit exhausted. Your plan covers a maximum of 20 outpatient rehabilitative therapy visits per calendar year." The notice lists denial code 119.

sections.heading: Why I am appealing
sections.text:
The denial rests on a visit count, not on the need for the care. Before I can agree that the limit applies, I need to see the exact plan language relied on and how the plan counted my visits.

I ask for the full text of the plan provision that sets the 20-visit limit, including any definition of "outpatient rehabilitative therapy" and any exceptions. A denial notice must state the specific reason and identify the plan provision relied on [[cite:fed.notice.required_content]].

I also ask for the visit-by-visit accounting the plan used: each date of service, provider, and code that was counted toward the 20 visits in calendar year 2026. I believe the count may be incorrect for these reasons: [ADD: your specific concerns, for example visits that were denied, canceled, billed by a different provider, or that were habilitative rather than rehabilitative]. I have received the following therapy in 2026: [ADD: list of your therapy dates and providers].

If any visits counted toward the limit fall under a different benefit, the claim should be reprocessed under the correct benefit. I ask the plan to confirm the meaning of the codes used on this claim, including code 119 and CPT 97110 [[cite:fed.claim_file.codes_meaning]].

My treating provider supports continued care. I am enclosing or will forward a supporting statement from [ADD: treating provider name and credentials] describing my condition and the reason these visits were ordered.

sections.heading: What I am asking for
sections.text:
1. A complete copy of the claim file and every document, record, rule, guideline, and protocol used in deciding this claim, free of charge [[cite:fed.claim_file.free_copies]].

2. The exact plan provision applied, any internal criterion used, and the name and credentials of the person who reviewed the claim [[cite:fed.notice.required_content]].

3. A written decision on this appeal within the time frame required for care already received [[cite:fed.internal_appeal.decision_windows]].

4. The plan's full calculation of my 2026 visit count, with each date and code counted toward the 20-visit maximum [[cite:fed.claim_file.free_copies]].

5. The meaning of each diagnosis and treatment code applied to this claim [[cite:fed.claim_file.codes_meaning]].

6. Reprocessing of claim CLM-26-0904-11907 under the correct benefit if the count or benefit category is wrong.

I can be reached at [ADD: your phone number] or [ADD: your email address]. Written correspondence may be sent to the address above. If the plan does not follow the required claims procedure, I may be treated as having completed the internal appeal [[cite:fed.deemed_exhaustion]]. I reserve the right to request an independent external review after the plan's decision, which is due within the applicable time limit [[cite:fed.external_review.decision_windows]].

Respectfully,

[ADD: your full name]
Member ID: SCH-71133820
